title: Employer Funding Deposits by ACH Credit — Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service Desk Tool Reference
content:
## The funding deposit

This rule settles the funding deposit an employer sends by its own ACH credit to bring a Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service with automatic replenishment on up to its funding level. Sending the funding deposit is the employer's own payment from its own bank account: the desk works out the deposit, the authorized employer contact sends it in person, and the credit is booked as one deposit made by employer ACH credit and marked as sent by the employer on the day it is sent.

Before a funding deposit is worked out, the alert level on file must stand at the replenishment floor. While the alert level on file stands anywhere other than at the replenishment floor, no funding deposit is worked out.

A funding deposit is not quoted until the ledger carries the automatic replenishment debit that the balance's fall below the alert level on file makes due. While the service's ledger does not yet show that automatic replenishment debit, no funding deposit is quoted.

## Sending the deposit

The deposit is sent with `send_prefund_ach_credit_62da4f1e`, a tool the customer themselves runs: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the employer's authorized contact runs it in person.

**Capability.** The employer's authorized contact sends, from the employer's own bank account, an ACH credit that prefunds the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service. One call books one prefund deposit dated today, made by employer ACH credit and marked as sent by the employer, and raises the service's prefund balance by the amount; the employer sees the deposit on its ledger at once, and the money can be paid out once the tier's ACH availability period has passed.

### Parameters

- `disburse_service_id` — the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, as read to the employer by the desk from the service record (identifier).
- `amount` — the amount the employer sends, in US dollars as a positive number with exactly 2 decimal places; a value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before booking.

### Return

- A one-line confirmation naming the new ledger entry reference (text), the service reference (text), the entry date (YYYY-MM-DD), the ordinal of the deposit among the service's deposits booked that day (integer), the amount credited (US dollars, two decimals) and the prefund balance after the credit (US dollars, two decimals). The entry reference being present means the deposit was booked.
- A message beginning "Not booked" means the amount was not greater than zero and nothing changed.

### Contract illustration (hypothetical values)

An `amount` of 512.3449 books a deposit of 512.34; an `amount` of 0 returns a message beginning "Not booked".
